ability.name: Step 1 - Determine local network range
ability.description: Read subnets and IP interfaces to calculate target CIDR block.

stages.command_template: $d='C:\Windows\Temp\bas'; if(!(Test-Path $d)){ni -ItemType Directory -Force $d|out-null}; $(try { $adapters = Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notlike '127.*' -and $_.PrefixLength -lt 32 }; if ($adapters) { $cidrList = @(); foreach ($adapter in $adapters) { $ipBytes = ([System.Net.IPAddress]$adapter.IPAddress).GetAddressBytes(); $maskBytes = [System.BitConverter]::GetBytes([uint32]([Math]::Pow(2,32)-[Math]::Pow(2,32-$adapter.PrefixLength))); if ([BitConverter]::IsLittleEndian) { [Array]::Reverse($maskBytes) }; $netBytes = 0..3 | ForEach-Object { $ipBytes[$_] -band $maskBytes[$_] }; $net = $netBytes -join '.'; $cidr = "$net/$($adapter.PrefixLength)"; $cidrList += $cidr; Write-Output "CIDR: $cidr" }; $cidrList | Out-File "$d\network_cidrs.txt" -Encoding ascii; $cidrList[0] | Out-File "$d\network_cidr.txt" -Encoding ascii } else { Write-Output "ERROR: No suitable adapters found" } } catch { "ERROR: $_" }) | Tee-Object -FilePath $d\step1.txt

rationale: Derives CIDR dynamically from adapter configurations so that network sweeps stay strictly within the assigned network scopes.
